daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo Subianto summoned party leaders to Bogor Palace to gather input on selecting a new vice president following Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation. Political parties discussed criteria for an ideal vice president but unanimously declined to submit candidate names, a move analysts interpret as demonstrating loyalty to Prabowo. The MPR is preparing to hold a vice presidential election and has formed a verification team, with PKS stating it does not want the diploma issue to recur.

  • Analysts noted that because Gibran is not a party cadre, Prabowo has greater flexibility in choosing his replacement.
  • On his first day without the vice presidential title, Gibran prayed Friday prayers with residents in Gandaria, South Jakarta, where he was mobbed by children.
  • Gibran and his family remain guarded by the Presidential Security Detail (Paspampres) despite his resignation.
  • A new lawsuit has been filed at the Constitutional Court seeking to eliminate the high school diploma requirement for presidential and vice presidential candidates, with petitioners citing that U.S. presidential candidates face no diploma requirement.
  • Political analyst Ganjar Pranowo responded to Gibran's admission that he disappointed PDI-P when he ran as Prabowo's running mate.
  • The suspect in the case involving Jokowi's diploma, Rizal Fadillah, died, according to reports from Jakarta.
  • Police Professional Standards Division examined Brigadier General TK in connection with the wiretapping case involving President Prabowo.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Brazil are exploring a partnership on tropical forest financing and carbon certification at the COP31 climate conference, marking closer environmental cooperation between the two major tropical forest nations. The collaboration focuses on mechanisms to fund forest conservation and establish carbon credit frameworks.

  • Indonesia is scheduled to sign the ASEAN digital economy agreement on November 14 in Manila.
  • Indonesia and Russia signed a memorandum of understanding on business competition policy cooperation.
  • Indonesian citizens have been recruited as Russian mercenaries under what are described as death-bound contracts.
  • Germany's ambassador stated that Germany views Indonesia as a potential partner to strengthen economic resilience.

Other

Coordinating Economic Minister Airlangga Hartarto expressed optimism about Indonesia's 2027 economic outlook, while President Prabowo separately received reports showing economic growth of 5.47 percent and inflation at 3.3 percent. Vice President Muhaimin Iskandar called for economic reforms to strengthen small businesses.

  • The government has extended the halal certification deadline to October 2028.
  • Indonesia targets December completion of the review process for Whoosh high-speed rail share transfers.
  • The government assured that BYD's local hiring share is fair amid scrutiny of the Chinese automaker's employment practices.
  • Indonesia seeks stronger protection for its media industry.
  • President Prabowo awarded honors to forest fire volunteers who died or were injured in the line of duty, with Minister Sugiono pledging the state will guarantee the future of their families.
